statement: Colten Ellis was born on October 5, 2000.
Colten Ellis is a Canadian professional ice hockey player.
Colten Ellis is a goaltender for the Buffalo Sabres of the National Hockey League (NHL).
Colten Ellis was selected 93rd overall by the St. Louis Blues in the third round of the 2019 NHL entry draft.
Ellis was born and raised in River Denys, Nova Scotia.
Ellis emerged as one of Atlantic Canada's top young goaltenders while playing for the Cape Breton West Islanders.
Ellis led the Cape Breton West Islanders and the province to its first-ever Telus Cup in 2017.
Ellis played major junior hockey in the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL) with the Cape Breton Screaming Eagles, the Rimouski Océanic, and the Charlottetown Islanders.
During his time in the QMJHL, Ellis earned defensive rookie of the year in his first year.
During his time in the QMJHL, Ellis earned a spot on the all-rookie team in his first year.
Ellis was selected by the St. Louis Blues with the 93rd overall pick in the 2019 NHL entry draft.
In his final QMJHL season, Ellis tied the career QMJHL shutout record.
In his final QMJHL season, Ellis broke the best goals-against-average season record.
In his final QMJHL season, Ellis had the fourth-best season save percentage all time.
Ellis was named the best goaltender of the year.
Ellis earned a spot on the first all-star team.
Ellis signed an entry-level contract with St. Louis in 2021.
Ellis spent several seasons developing within the St. Louis organization after signing his contract.
Ellis began his professional career with the ECHL's Worcester Railers.
Ellis earned opportunities with the American Hockey League (AHL) Springfield Thunderbirds.
A mid-season injury sidelined Ellis for the rest of the 2022–23 season with the ECHL Tulsa Oilers.
Ellis's statistics and play improved in the seasons following his injury.
Ellis eventually earned the Thunderbirds' starting role.
In October 2025, the Blues placed Ellis on waivers.
Ellis was claimed by the Buffalo Sabres in October 2025.
Ellis made his NHL debut in October 2025.
Ellis became the first goaltender from Cape Breton Island to play in the NHL.
Internationally, Ellis has represented the Canada national team.
Ellis was born in River Denys, Nova Scotia on October 5, 2000.
Ellis's parents are Jo-Ann and Brian Ellis.
Ellis is one of three children in his family.
Ellis began playing hockey with the Whycocomagh Minor Hockey Association.
Ellis has one brother, Matt.
Ellis has one cousin, Chase, who played in the QMJHL with him.
Ellis joined the Nova Junior X-Men of the Nova Scotia Under-15 Major Hockey League in the 2013–14 season.
Ellis stayed with the Nova Junior X-Men for the 2014–15 season.
Ellis had a 2.08 goals against average (GAA) in the 2013–14 season with the Nova Junior X-Men.
Ellis had a 1.61 GAA in the 2014–15 season with the Nova Junior X-Men.
Following two seasons with the X-Men, Ellis joined the Cape Breton West Islanders of the Nova Scotia Under-18 Major Hockey League for the 2015–16 season.
Ellis put up a .890 save percentage with the Cape Breton West Islanders in the 2015–16 season.
Ellis put up a 3.70 GAA with the Cape Breton West Islanders in the 2015–16 season.
The Cape Breton Screaming Eagles selected Ellis in the fourth round of the 2016 Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL) entry draft with the 59th overall pick.
Ellis attended the Screaming Eagles training camp.
Ellis was assigned back to the Islanders after attending the Screaming Eagles training camp.
Ellis brought the Islanders to winning the provincial championship.
The Islanders were entered into the Atlantic Region Telus Cup qualifier.
The Islanders beat out the Moncton Flyers to earn a spot in the Telus Cup.
The Islanders became the first Nova Scotia team to win the Telus Cup.
Ellis made 43 saves in the final game of the Telus Cup.
Ellis had an overtime breakaway in the final game of the Telus Cup.
Ellis had a 2.20 GAA in the Telus Cup tournament.
Ellis had a .929 save percentage in the Telus Cup tournament.
Ellis was called up to the Screaming Eagles throughout the 2016–17 QMJHL season.
Ellis played three games with the Screaming Eagles in the 2016–17 QMJHL season.
Ellis had a 2–0–0 record with the Screaming Eagles in the 2016–17 QMJHL season.
Ellis had a 2.50 GAA with the Screaming Eagles in the 2016–17 QMJHL season.
Ellis had an .885 save percentage with the Screaming Eagles in the 2016–17 QMJHL season.
On June 3, 2017, Ellis was traded to the Rimouski Océanic for a first-round pick in the 2018 QMJHL entry draft.
Ellis began the 2017–18 QMJHL season in Rimouski along with goaltender Jimmy Lemay.
Ellis played 51 games for the Rimouski Océanic in the 2017–18 QMJHL season.
Ellis led the Océanic to the QMJHL playoffs in the 2017–18 season.
In the 2017–18 QMJHL playoffs, the Rimouski Océanic faced the Moncton Wildcats in the first round.
The Rimouski Océanic lost to the Moncton Wildcats in seven games in the 2017–18 QMJHL playoffs.
Ellis ended his rookie QMJHL season first in wins with 33.
Ellis ended his rookie QMJHL season first in shutouts with 6.
Ellis was third in goals against average with 2.35 GAA in his rookie QMJHL season.
Ellis was third in save percentage with .913% in his rookie QMJHL season.
Ellis was nominated for the RDS Cup, the QMJHL rookie of the year award.
Ellis was nominated for the Raymond Lagacé Trophy, the defensive rookie of the year award.
Alexis Lafrenière won the RDS Cup.
Ellis won the Raymond Lagacé Trophy.
Ellis was named to the All-Rookie team.
Ellis was named to the second All-Star team.
Rimouski continued to have Ellis as the starting goaltender beginning the 2018–19 season.
Ellis was one of 40 players selected for the 2019 CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game.
Ellis played just under 30 minutes in net at the 2019 CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game.
Ellis saved 15 out of 17 shots on goal at the 2019 CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game.
By the end of the 2018–19 season, Ellis was ranked eighth across all North American goaltenders for the 2019 NHL entry draft.
Ellis recorded a 2.47 GAA in 46 games during the 2018–19 season.
Ellis recorded a .910 save percentage in 46 games during the 2018–19 season.
Rimouski entered the 2019 playoffs as the third seed in the eastern conference.
Rimouski beat out the Chicoutimi Saguenéens and the Screaming Eagles in the 2019 playoffs.
Rimouski was swept by the Rouyn-Noranda Huskies in the 2019 semi-finals.
Ellis played 12 games in the 2019 playoffs.
Ellis had a 2.36 GAA in the 2019 playoffs.
Ellis had a .919 save percentage in the 2019 playoffs.
The St. Louis Blues selected Ellis in the third round with the 93rd overall pick in the 2019 NHL entry draft.
Ellis was returned to Rimouski for the 2019–20 season after being drafted.
Ellis played in September and October of the 2019–20 season.
Ellis sustained an injury that required surgery in the 2019–20 season.
The injury prevented Ellis from playing in November and December of the 2019–20 season.
At the time of his injury, Ellis had played 14 games.
At the time of his injury, Ellis had a 2.61 GAA.
At the time of his injury, Ellis had a .905 save percentage.
On March 12, the QMJHL season was suspended for a week due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The QMJHL season was cancelled for the rest of the season on March 18.
Ellis had played 29 games when the 2019–20 QMJHL season ended.
Ellis had a 2.41 GAA when the 2019–20 QMJHL season ended.
Ellis had a .904 save percentage when the 2019–20 QMJHL season ended.
Following the end of the 2019–20 season, the Charlottetown Islanders traded for Ellis.
The Charlottetown Islanders gave up a 2020 third-round pick, and a 2021 first- and second-round pick to trade for Ellis.
The 2020–21 season for the Ontario Hockey League was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
The Western Hockey League started delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic in the 2020–21 season.
The 2020–21 QMJHL season continued as normal.
Ellis started the 2020–21 season with a spot on the Week 3 QMJHL Team of the Week on October 19.
Ellis recorded a shutout against the Halifax Mooseheads on October 19.
On March 1, 2021, Ellis signed his three-year, entry-level contract with the Blues.
Ellis's entry-level contract with the Blues began in the 2021–22 NHL season.
On March 22, Ellis set the all-time QMJHL record for shutouts by a goaltender with eighteen.
Ellis shut out the Screaming Eagles 4–0 on March 22.
Ellis was named Player of the Week on March 22.
Ellis recorded two shutouts in the week ending March 22.
By the end of the 2020–21 season, Ellis had seven shutouts.
Ellis's seven shutouts tied the single-season shutout record at the time.
The single-season shutout record was held by six goalies, including Roberto Luongo.
Roberto Luongo is a Hockey Hall of Fame inductee.
Ellis had a record of 23–1–0 in the 2020–21 season.
Ellis had a 1.78 GAA in the 2020–21 season.
Ellis had a .926 save percentage in the 2020–21 season.
Ellis set the lowest GAA for a season by a goaltender in the QMJHL.
Ellis had the fourth-best all-time save percentage in the QMJHL.
Ellis received the Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy for best goaltender for his performance in the 2020–21 regular season.
Ellis earned a spot on the First All-Star team for his performance in the 2020–21 regular season.
Ellis led the Islanders to the semi-finals of the playoffs against the Victoriaville Tigres.
The Islanders lost the series 2–3 to the Victoriaville Tigres in the semi-finals.
By the 2021–22 season, Ellis had aged out of the QMJHL.
Ellis began his professional career in the 2021–22 season.
Ellis participated in the Blues' preseason training camp in the 2021–22 season.
Ellis was assigned to the Worcester Railers in the ECHL.
Ellis made his professional debut on October 23 against the Maine Mariners.
Ellis's professional debut was a 4–3 win.
Ellis saved 42 out of 45 shots on goal in his professional debut.
On October 30, Ellis was called up to the American Hockey League (AHL) Springfield Thunderbirds.
Ellis made his AHL debut against the Bridgeport Islanders.
Ellis saved 28 out of 29 shots on goal in his AHL debut.
Ellis's AHL debut was a 4–1 win.
Ellis was sent down to the Railers the day after his AHL debut.
On December 9, Ellis was called up again to the Thunderbirds.
Ellis stayed with the Thunderbirds for almost two months after being called up on December 9.
Ellis was sent down to the Railers for the final time on January 22.
Ellis played six games with the Thunderbirds in the 2021–22 season.
Ellis recorded a 1–3–2 record with the Thunderbirds in the 2021–22 season.
Ellis recorded a 3.93 GAA with the Thunderbirds in the 2021–22 season.
Ellis recorded a .880 save percentage with the Thunderbirds in the 2021–22 season.
On March 18, Ellis recorded his first professional shutout against the South Carolina Stingrays.
Ellis's first professional shutout was a 3–0 win.
Ellis made 23 saves in his first professional shutout.
By the end of the 2021–22 season, Ellis played 34 games with the Railers.
Ellis had a 15–13–5 record with the Railers in the 2021–22 season.
Ellis had a 3.21 GAA with the Railers in the 2021–22 season.
Ellis had a .905 save percentage with the Railers in the 2021–22 season.
Entering the 2022–23 ECHL season, Ellis participated in the Blues' Traverse City prospect tournament.
Ellis made the Thunderbirds opening roster for the 2022–23 season.
Joel Hofer made the Thunderbirds opening roster for the 2022–23 season.
Vadim Zherenko made the Thunderbirds opening roster for the 2022–23 season.
Ellis was assigned to the ECHL Tulsa Oilers on October 29.
Ellis took over as the Oilers starting goaltender following his reassignment.
Ellis started suffering issues with his hip in December while with the Oilers.
Ellis had season-ending hip surgery in February.
At the time of surgery, Ellis had finished the season with a 12–9–5 record.
Ellis had a 3.46 GAA at the time of surgery.
Ellis had an .888 save percentage at the time of surgery.
Ellis played 27 games at the time of surgery.
Ellis began his recovery period in February.
Ellis was back on the ice in June.
Prior to the 2023–24 ECHL season, Ellis participated in the Blues' training camp.
Ellis suffered a concussion at the Blues' training camp prior to the 2023–24 ECHL season.
Ellis was assigned to the Orlando Solar Bears to start the 2023–24 season.
Ellis had a record of 5–0–0 with the Orlando Solar Bears in December.
Ellis recorded one shutout with the Orlando Solar Bears in December.
Ellis had a 1.58 GAA with the Orlando Solar Bears in December.
Ellis had a .954 save percentage with the Orlando Solar Bears in December.
Ellis was named ECHL Goaltender of the Month for December.
Ellis was named ECHL Goaltender of the Week ending December 23.
Ellis had 2 wins in the week ending December 23.
Ellis had a 1.00 GAA in the week ending December 23.
Ellis had a .973 save percentage in the week ending December 23.
Thunderbirds goalie Vadim Zherenko suffered an injury in January.
Ellis was called up to the Thunderbirds on January 21.
Ellis played 13 games with the Thunderbirds while Zherenko was out.
Ellis recorded a 2.86 GAA with the Thunderbirds while Zherenko was out.
Ellis recorded a .926 save percentage with the Thunderbirds while Zherenko was out.
Malcolm Subban was traded to the Columbus Blue Jackets in March.
Zherenko and Ellis became the Thunderbirds goaltender tandem for the rest of the season.
Ellis played three more games for a season total of 2.89 GAA.
Ellis played three more games for a season total of .924 save percentage.
On June 11, Ellis signed a one-year, two-way contract extension worth $775,000 with the Blues.
Ellis started the 2024–25 season by participating in the Blues' training camp.
Ellis was assigned to the Thunderbirds to start the 2024–25 season.
Zherenko started in the Thunderbirds net on opening night of the 2024–25 season.
Ellis played 8 out of 12 games from the start of the 2024–25 season to mid-November.
Ellis had a .919 save percentage from the start of the 2024–25 season to mid-November.
Ellis had a 2.80 GAA from the start of the 2024–25 season to mid-November.
Ellis continued to be the Thunderbirds' starting goaltender after a strong start to the AHL season.
On March 6, Ellis signed a two-year, two-way contract extension worth $1.55 million with the Blues.
Ellis was named AHL Player of the Week ending March 9.
Ellis recorded a shutout in the week ending March 9.
Ellis made 95 saves in the week ending March 9.
Ellis had a 0.72 GAA in the week ending March 9.
Ellis had a .979 save percentage in the week ending March 9.
By the end of the 2024–25 season, Ellis had played 42 games.
Ellis had a 22–14–5 record in the 2024–25 season.
Ellis had a 2.63 GAA in the 2024–25 season.
Ellis had a .922 save percentage in the 2024–25 season.
The Thunderbirds entered the 2025 Calder Cup playoffs as the A6 seed.
The Thunderbirds were paired against the A3 seed Providence Bruins in the 2025 Calder Cup playoffs.
The Thunderbirds lost the series in three games in the 2025 Calder Cup playoffs.
Ellis recorded a 2.32 GAA in the 2025 Calder Cup playoffs.
Ellis recorded a .933 save percentage in the 2025 Calder Cup playoffs.
Following the Calder Cup playoffs, Ellis was called up to the Blues on April 28.
Ellis did not appear in any Stanley Cup playoff games.
Before the start of the 2025–26 NHL season on October 5, the Blues put Ellis on waivers.
Ellis was claimed by the Sabres the day after being placed on waivers.
Ellis and Alexandar Georgiev were in contention for the backup spot to start the 2025–26 season behind Alex Lyon.
Georgiev was waived the day after Ellis was claimed by the Sabres.
Ellis became the backup to Lyon to start the 2025–26 season.
Ellis made his NHL debut on October 22 in a 4–2 win against the Detroit Red Wings.
Ellis saved 27 out of 29 shots on goal in his NHL debut.
Ellis became the first goaltender from Cape Breton Island to play in the NHL.
Ellis became the eighth goaltender from Nova Scotia to play in the NHL.
Ellis became the ninth Sabres goaltender to win in their debut.
Ellis was selected as a goaltender for the 2018 IIHF World U18 Championships.
Olivier Rodrigue was selected as a goaltender for the 2018 IIHF World U18 Championships.
Ellis started the first two round-robin games at the 2018 IIHF World U18 Championships against the United States and Belarus.
Ellis recorded a 3.50 GAA at the 2018 IIHF World U18 Championships.
Ellis recorded a .887 save percentage at the 2018 IIHF World U18 Championships.
Olivier Rodrigue took over the starting goaltender role for Team Canada at the 2018 IIHF World U18 Championships.
Team Canada lost to the Czech Republic in quarterfinals play at the 2018 IIHF World U18 Championships.
Ellis did not make the December camp roster cut for the 2020 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships roster for Canada.
On December 20, 2024, Hockey Canada announced their roster for the 2024 Spengler Cup.
Ellis was selected as a goaltender for the 2024 Spengler Cup roster.
Antoine Bibeau was selected as a goaltender for the 2024 Spengler Cup roster.
At the time of his selection for the 2024 Spengler Cup, Ellis had an 8–4–2 record.
At the time of his selection for the 2024 Spengler Cup, Ellis had a 2.70 GAA.
At the time of his selection for the 2024 Spengler Cup, Ellis had a .918 save percentage.
Ellis started the 2024 Spengler Cup tournament in net against HC Davos.
Ellis recorded 25 saves in a 6–2 win against HC Davos at the 2024 Spengler Cup.
Ellis continued to be the starting goaltender for Team Canada at the 2024 Spengler Cup.
Ellis played two more games at the 2024 Spengler Cup before losing to the Straubing Tigers in the semifinals.
Ellis finished the 2024 Spengler Cup tournament with a 2.68 GAA.
Ellis finished the 2024 Spengler Cup tournament with a .911 save percentage.
Ellis's 2.68 GAA and .911 save percentage were the second-best in the 2024 Spengler Cup tournament.
Luca Hollenstein was the HC Davos goaltender.
Ellis won the Raymond Lagacé Trophy in 2018.
Ellis was named to the All-Rookie Team in 2018.
Ellis was named to the Second All-Star Team in 2018.
Ellis won the Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy in 2021.
Ellis was named to the First All-Star Team in 2021.
